summary.headline: STL posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of INR2,529 crore (+145% YoY) and raised its FY29 EBITDA margin target to about 30% from 27%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a second consecutive record quarter for revenue, operational EBITDA and PAT, with reported EBITDA of INR846 crore including a one-off INR161 crore US tariff refund gain. Operational EBITDA was INR685 crore (27.1% margin), up 624 bps QoQ, driven by higher utilisation, richer mix and more data-centre and attach-rate revenue. Open order book reached a record INR35,274 crore, with H1 orders of about INR32,000 crore. Management kept the FY29 revenue target at INR20,000 crore but lifted the FY29 EBITDA margin target to about 30%. Spot business is now negligible, so revenue is increasingly drawn from scheduled backlog.

guidance_outlook: FY29 (Lakshya) EBITDA margin target raised to about 30% from 27%; FY29 revenue target kept at INR20,000 crore (about 4x FY26).
Management aims to perform at or above the Q2 operational margin of 27% from Q3 FY27 onwards.
Net working capital cycle to stay in the 45-50 day range; debtor and inventory improvement expected from next quarter.
Net finance cost expected to fall from Q3 FY27 after early loan prepayments.
Capex of about INR1,000 crore per year from FY27 to FY29, for a 50% expansion of preform, fiber and cable capacity and a greenfield preterm solutions facility.
R&D commitment of 2% of annual revenue for next-generation optical platforms.
risks_watch: Q2 reported EBITDA includes a one-off INR161 crore tariff refund gain; operational margin of 27.1% is the true base.
Supply-constrained raw materials (germanium, helium) and lower payable days; working capital cycle is at the upper end of the 45-50 day range.
Execution risk on the INR35,274 crore order book from hyperscaler capex timing, interest rates, and local land, power and water constraints.
Customer concentration in hyperscaler contracts; management did not disclose the attach-rate contribution or the DC fiber revenue split.
Hollow-core and multi-core fiber commercial scale-up is 1.5-2 years away, so near-term revenue from these is limited.
Interest cost rose 15% YoY in Q2 with receivables up; management expects lower net finance cost from Q3 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, order book and margin trajectory, with the margin upgrade tied to the order book and mix. Management was evasive on pricing, utilisation percentages, DC attach revenue and attach-rate targets, citing competitive reasons.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin target upgrade to 30% while the INR20,000 crore revenue target was kept, and is a revenue target upgrade possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the upgrade reflects the INR35,000 crore order book, a mix shift toward higher-margin data center products and a higher attach rate. The INR20,000 crore revenue target is retained, to be re-evaluated against order book execution and capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Reported EBITDA includes a INR161 crore US tariff refund; is more refund expected, and why did interest cost rise 15% YoY with receivables up, plus the INR49 crore impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Most refunds have been received; Phase 3 is in process and a small amount has been applied for. The INR49 crore impairment and INR22 crore extra depreciation relate to subsidiary Speedon Networks, squared off in full. Some loans were prepaid early with penalties settled, and net finance cost is expected to fall from Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DC fiber revenue and DC attach revenue contribution, and is attach revenue part of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split DC fiber or DC attach revenue, citing competitive reasons. It confirmed that attach-rate revenue (accessories business) forms part of the reported order book. A good portion of the order book is DC, given the two large deals announced.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 margins be better than the 27% Q2 level, given H1 margin of about 23-24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to perform at or above the Q2 operational margin of 27% from Q3 FY27, and that the Lakshya plan aligns with the 30% FY29 target. Margin gains are attributed to the DC-heavy mix, which is more profitable than traditional Telco business.

qa_highlights.question: What is average utilisation and when will full utilisation be reached? Also, where does the company stand on DC share versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose utilisation figures; it said utilisation is improving quarter on quarter after better raw material procurement and diversification. On DC share, management reiterated a target of about 50%, with 50-60% by design, and said it is cutting low-end commoditised fiber and cable sales.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to order book delivery timelines given US and global AI data center project delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is watching interest rates and hyperscaler cash positions, and flagged local execution challenges around land, power, water and local opposition. It said conversations have not changed, and hyperscalers are diversifying into the Nordics, India, Australia and Mongolia.

capex_capacity: Capex of about INR1,000 crore per year from FY27 to FY29, covering brownfield expansion of preform, fiber and cable capacity by 50% and a greenfield preterm solutions facility (CFO said total capex INR1,000 crore per year, 2027 to 2029).
Management said it is building a new greenfield site to increase termination capability, as part of the capex plan.
Utilisation is improving quarter on quarter after easing raw material constraints (germanium, helium); management did not give utilisation percentages.
Management wants to start executing capacity projects and bring them online in the next few quarters, and expects capacity coming up in the next 2 to 3 years to support further partnerships.
Hollow-core and multi-core fiber scale-up expected in roughly 1.5 to 2 years; HCF is in first commercial pilot phase.
demand_pricing: Order intake in H1 FY27 was about INR32,000 crore, roughly 4x the orders won in all of FY26; largest Q2 win is a new 5-year agreement with a potential value of $1.2 billion from a global hyperscaler for AI-ready optical solutions, following a $1.11 billion award last quarter.

Open order book INR35,274 crore, up 4.6x from INR7,687 crore at start of FY27; about INR3,021 crore scheduled for Q3 FY27, rest in Q4 FY27 and beyond. Order book spread across customer segments, product categories and geographies.
Spot business now a negligible share of revenue; revenue increasingly drawn from scheduled multiyear backlog with hyperscalers and telecom operators.
Data Center share was 33% of H1 FY27 revenue; management targets about 50% in the current fiscal and a 50-60% DC share by design. A good portion of the order book is DC-linked.
Global ex-China OFC market share rose to 9% in H1 FY27 from 7% in H1 FY26. Attach rate reached 24% in H1 FY27 vs 20% in H1 FY26, on a much larger OFC revenue base; target is 25% and beyond for FY27.
Market context cited from CRU: global optical cable demand expected to reach 851 million fiber km by 2031 (7.5% CAGR); CRU upgraded 2026 data center demand growth to 89% YoY from 63%.
Pricing: management declined to comment on prices, preform or fiber price trends, citing competitive reasons; focus is on high-end Neuralis cables and connectivity products (CONCAT, MMC).
Management did not disclose attach-rate contribution or DC fiber revenue split, citing competitive reasons.
